facts.text: The controllers launch loads the gripper controller configuration and spawns panda_simulator/panda_gripper_controller when load_gripper is true.

The gripper controller configuration uses type panda_sim_controllers/PandaGripperController, the pub_topic /franka_gripper/joint_states and the two finger joints panda_finger_joint1 and panda_finger_joint2.
The controller constructor initializes the homing, stop, move and grasp action servers on /franka_gripper/homing, /franka_gripper/stop, /franka_gripper/move and /franka_gripper/grasp.
init() starts the homing, stop, move and grasp action servers and creates a 0.1 s ROS timer that calls timerUpdate.
The controller includes franka_gripper/GraspAction.h, HomingAction.h, MoveAction.h and StopAction.h.

init() advertises sensor_msgs/JointState with queue size 1 and latch true on the pub_topic parameter through the private node handle when pub_topic is set, and otherwise on the absolute /franka_gripper/joint_states.
timerUpdate copies the two finger positions into the JointState message, sets zero velocities and zero efforts, sets no header field and publishes it.

The move handler clamps width/2 to the main finger joint's URDF lower and upper limits and the speed to plus or minus its URDF velocity limit, writes both command buffers, sets new_command_, then loops without sleeping for up to 5 s of ros::Time until the sum of the two absolute finger positions is within 0.01 of the goal width, and sets the goal succeeded or, on timeout, aborted.

The grasp handler applies the same clamping, command-buffer writes and 5 s ros::Time wait as move, reads only the goal's width and speed (not force or epsilon), and sets the goal succeeded or aborted.

The stop handler sets the position command buffer to half the sum of the two absolute measured finger positions and the speed command buffer to 0.0, sets new_command_, and then sets the goal succeeded with success true without any condition.

update() calls updateCommands() on every fifth call and updates both finger controllers on every call; updateCommands() returns at once unless new_command_ is set, and otherwise applies the buffered position and speed to the main finger and the URDF mimic multiplier and offset to the other finger.

Each finger's JointPositionController computes its effort command on every update from the position error and, when the command carries a velocity, from the difference between that velocity and the joint velocity.
The homing handler only logs 'Homing not implemented for simulator.' and sets no goal status itself.
The move wait loop compares ros::Time::now() minus its start time with the 5 s timeout and the measured width with the goal width, and contains no is_preempt_requested check.
The grasp wait loop compares ros::Time::now() minus its start time with the 5 s timeout and the measured width with the goal width, and contains no is_preempt_requested check.
The simulator configuration declares default_speed 0.1 m/s and default_grasp_epsilon inner/outer 0.005 m.
init() reads the default_speed parameter into a local variable initialized to 0.1 and logs it when the parameter is found.
panda_world.launch declares load_gripper and use_custom_action_servers with default true.
panda_world.launch declares use_sim_time with default true.
panda_world.launch starts start_gripper_action_server.py as gripper_action_server_emulator when use_custom_action_servers and load_gripper are true.

GripperActionServer serves control_msgs GripperCommandAction on the relative name franka_gripper/gripper_action and creates a franka_interface.GripperInterface for panda_finger_joint1 and panda_finger_joint2.

While a GripperCommand goal runs, its callback calls GripperInterface.move_joints with twice the goal position at a 20 Hz rospy.Rate until the first finger reaches the goal, a preemption is requested or the timeout passes.

determinism.notes: Event-driven ROS-free stand-in with no physics step or wall-clock pacing; its finger positions and action results are placeholders, not captured traffic

gaps: the fake is an analytic ROS-free stand-in built on RecordingRosTransport: it answers the declared gripper action and joint-state wire traffic but runs no Gazebo, ros_control, franka_interface or physics

the fake's finger positions and action results are placeholders; a successful move or grasp sets both placeholder finger positions to width/2 immediately, while the upstream handler waits up to 5 s of ROS time and clamps to the URDF limits
the upstream grasp handler ignores force and epsilon; the driver sends fixed zero values for those required goal fields and exposes no force input
the upstream homing handler sets no goal status itself and is not bound
the arm's seven-joint trajectory action, joint-command topic, arm state topics and MoveIt integration are NOT COVERED; the pinned clone has no acknowledged arm stop binding
the fake's stop result is synthesized; it does not prove physical quiescence or a hardware stop

the move and grasp waits run on ros::Time, which panda_world.launch makes simulated time by default: while Gazebo is paused a running goal does not end, and below a real-time factor of 0.5 an unreached goal can outlast the 10 s binding timeout and end as an unknown outcome

a running move or grasp goal ignores cancellation and the stop, so an e-stop during it reports MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held until the goal ends (reviewer probe and the hold_goals test case); the fake otherwise answers every goal at once

the hold lasts only until the next move or grasp goal: a goal another ROS client queued behind a running goal in the same action server, or the gripper_action_server_emulator that panda_world.launch starts by default (it re-commands the fingers at 20 Hz while its GripperCommand goal runs), replaces it; the MHS latch fences only this driver

the four action servers start in init() and keep answering while a controller switch has stopped the gripper controller, when update() applies no finger command; a stop is then acknowledged without effect

/franka_gripper/joint_states is latched and published by a ROS timer: while Gazebo is paused no new sample is published, so reads can wait and fail MHS.DEVICE.NOT_READY and each command then waits for the resource read (reviewer probe with a silent topic: 2 s); the JointState header is never set

the endpoint names are those of franka_ros's real franka_gripper node (franka_ros is listed in dependencies.rosinstall and is not in the clone): against a real Franka graph these bindings would drive the real hand, including grasps with the fixed zero force and epsilon
no ROS graph, Gazebo process, simulator run or hardware was executed or validated

safe_state.description: The /franka_gripper/stop action buffers a hold of the measured opening (half the sum of the absolute finger positions, zero speed target) and acknowledges success before the controller's next command update applies it; the finger PIDs then hold that opening while Gazebo and the arm keep running, a move or grasp goal still running ignores the stop for up to 5 s of ROS time (leaving the e-stop unconfirmed, latch held), and a later move or grasp goal from any ROS client replaces the hold.
